bindings.label: Episodes of continuous, low-amplitude, high-frequency jerking movements of all extremities with occasional neck and torso involvement

Patient is a 73-year-old woman with stage 4 chronic kidney disease and ischemic cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 15%-20%), presenting with acute decompensated heart failure; she was started on intravenous bumetanide and intravenous dobutamine at 2.5 mg/kg per hour.

Examination showed the jerking movements were generally synchronous, present both at rest and with stimulation, sometimes frequent enough to give the appearance of shivering; no fever or hypothermia was present.
Laboratory tests show markedly elevated BUN and creatinine
Laboratory tests show normal ionized calcium and magnesium
Patient's consciousness is preserved during the jerking episodes
EEG was not obtained to confirm triphasic waves or exclude non-convulsive seizures
Precise timing of bumetanide and dobutamine administration is unavailable
